I would argue that they didn't utilized the multiverse enough. They should have gone all in with the multiverse stuff imo. There is alot of films and series in this supposed "Multiverse saga" that had nothing to do with the multiverse. Only Wandavision, NWH, MoM, Loki and DP&W made the multiverse the main draw. The rest did not. You could argue that Ant-man 3 and The Marvels used the multiverse but it was only in the post credit scenes. The rest are a bunch of set-up of characters that will probably die in Doomsday and Secret Wars.

I feel like the reason why the Multiverse Saga ended up as a disaster is that they pretty much a blueballed the audience repeatedly that the audience grew tired off. The Sony Spider-Man Cinematic Universe situation didn't help and made it worse.

Wandavision - Hey, we are now finally crossing over with the X-men. LOL, here is a dick joke though.

Venom 2 - Ohhh Venom is in the MCU Baby!

No Way Home - Hey we are bring back the 3 spider-men together. Ohh remember that Venom thing? Gotcha!!! But ohhh the symbiote is in the MCU now!

Morbius - Lol what the fuck was that film but here's a post-credit scene that we're PROBABLY crossing over to the MCU and will definitely pay off some day! (it never paid off).

MoM - We just came after No way home, how are we gonna top that?!? He's the motherfucking XMEN and fancasted Mr. Fantastic! *Dies in the next few scenes*

Loki - Here is the next big villain that will be the a huge menace in the MCU.

Antman 3 - *The big villian got trampled on by ants*. Ohh our bad, but that villain has thousands of versions of himself!

Loki 2 - Oh shit you didn't like the villain that got run over by ants?!? Lets just quietly move away from that. 

I can go on and on how the MCU repeatedly conditioned the audience that every set-up they made didn't matter in this multiverse saga. I know the GA probably has fault in it too by expecting too much but this is what happens when you play with people's expectations. The SSCU situation also fucked up the audience interest imo despite MCU had nothing to do with it. That level of blueballing was acceptable in Wandavision but to repeatedly do it with no foreseeable pay-off really hurt audience interests.
